text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives management of Yugoslav airlines JAT on 70th anniversary of civil aviation and 50th anniversary of the airline.

- Croatia has still not responded to Yugoslav dual citizenship proposal, talks with Croatian side scheduled in three days on the issue and on 17 other agreements, said assistant Foreign Minister Zivadin Jovanovic.
- Banks should extend financial support to successful export-oriented production and not to all firms equally, including loss-makers, said Zivota Mihajlovic general manager of Vojvodjanska Banka.

- Serbian tobacco industry is facing collapse due to smuggling - the Nis tobacco factory DIN has shut down its plants while half of the workers in the Vranje tobacco industry DIV have been sent on compulsory leave.
- Serbian government has invested maximum efforts to ensure all that is necessary for spring sowing, so far 300,000 hectares have been sown.

- Serbian government discusses realisation of its programme for renewal of agricultural machinery. By end of June 2,200 tractors, 1,030 motocultivators, 150 combines, 220 harvesters, and 3850 other agricultural machines to be produced.

- The second working version of the Serbian information law will be presented by the end of the week and the draft will be submitted to parliament by early May, says Information Minister Radmila Milentijevic.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian government to discuss Wednesday the demand for price increase of power and fuels submitted by Serbian power company EPS and oil industry NIS.
- Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) appoints member of executive board Ivica Dacic to attend Serbia-Kosovo Albanian talks scheduled in New York on April 7-9.
- Montenegrin government to discuss privatisation plans Wednesday.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno leaders will ask for U.S. support in implementation of the OSCE Gonzalez report, says Serbian Renewal Movement leader Vuk Draskovic ahead of visit to Washington.
- There may be changes in Yugoslavia's import taxes in early June, says finance ministry official Veljko Golubovic.
- The Vrsac beer factory is facing recievership proceedings.
- Novi Sad construction firms to stage protest rally over constant increase of prices of public services.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT to be transformed into a holding company in which the state will have a majority stake, says directdor Zika Petrovic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic should decide by Thursday about request of the Democratic Party of Socialists main board to reconstruct his government.

- Serbian truck producer FAP does not intend to sue Mercedes-Benz over an agreement concluded until 1999 but cancelled when war broke out in the former Yugoslavia. "Our future coperation must go in a different direction," said FAP director Svetomir Papic.
- Opposition Civic Alliance (GSS) has serious objections to the draft privatisation law, GSS representatives said during talks with ownership transformation minister Milan Beko.
BORBA
- The Serbian government will form working groups for return of frozen foreign currency savings and for rehabilitation of the banking system, says ownership transformation minister Milan Beko.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin pensioners to receive second part of their February pensions on Wednesday, highest pension 1,319 dinars lowest 349 dinars.
- Student party members fully support president of National Party Novak Kilibarda, said chairman of the party's student organisation Predrag Ivanovic.
- Bar municipality will resume publishing local paper Barske novine.
- The 800 workers of the Podgorica construction machine factory Radoje Dakic go on strike demanding responsibility for those who brought the factory to its present chaotic situation.
- Porspecting completed for a new large source of drinking water in Tusko polje on the outskirts of Podgorica. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
